**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Transportation of Amara Okafor**  
**To:** Mrs. Okafor  
**Copy:** Darlene, Supervisor; Transportation Office  
**From:** [Your Name], Driver, Bus 41, Route 9  
**Date:** [Date submitted]  
**Re:** Complaint dated October 29

Dear Mrs. Okafor:

I am submitting this statement in response to your complaint dated October 29, which my supervisor, Darlene, provided to me on November 3. I understand that this statement will be kept in my record and that a copy will be provided to you. I want to explain what happened during the afternoon elementary run on Tuesday, October 27, why Amara remained on the bus, and how she was returned to Fairmont Elementary.

First, I understand that it would have been frightening to expect your kindergartner at her stop and then find that she was still on the bus. I have grandchildren, and I can understand how upsetting that uncertainty would be. I am sorry for the worry and difficult afternoon you experienced. I also want to be clear that my decision to keep Amara on the bus was made to follow the district’s dismissal rule and keep her safely supervised.

Amara has a green tag on her bag indicating that an adult must be present at the stop for her to be released. Under the district rule for kindergarten riders, if an adult is not present, the student must remain on the bus and be returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. That was the procedure I followed.

On October 27, I arrived at the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at approximately 3:52 p.m. The scheduled arrival time is 3:50 p.m. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult at the corner to receive Amara. Because I could not identify an adult waiting for her, I did not allow her to leave the bus.

At 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch about the situation. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 children on the bus. I continued the route before returning Amara to Fairmont Elementary. We arrived at the school at approximately 4:31 p.m. I personally walked Amara into the office and turned her over to Mrs. Petrakis.

I understand from your complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I cannot say whether that truck blocked my view of you, but I can state that I did not see or recognize an adult there waiting for Amara. I was not knowingly ignoring you, and I did not deliberately refuse to respond.

My decision was based on what I could see at the stop at the time. With a kindergarten student whose tag requires an adult to receive her, I could not release her without being able to identify that adult. I also could not leave the other children unattended on the bus to walk across the road and look for someone. My responsibility was to keep all of the children supervised while following the required procedure for Amara.

I also want to address the statement that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing. As we pulled away, I was directing a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I was attending to a student’s behavior as the bus began moving, not laughing at you or at the situation. I recognize that you may have understood what you saw differently, but I want the record to accurately reflect what I was doing.

During the remainder of the ride, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her that we were going on a little extra trip. My intention was to reassure her while we completed the remaining stops and returned to school. I do not offer this to minimize your concern. I include it to explain what I observed and how I spoke with her while she remained in my care.

I respectfully request that the Transportation Office promptly preserve and review the available bus camera footage from that afternoon, including any available audio. The review should include our arrival and wait at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street, our departure from the stop, and the return to Fairmont Elementary. That footage may help clarify the visibility at the stop, my interaction with the student in seat 2, and Amara’s time on the bus. I believe it is important for the complaint and my response to be considered alongside any available recording.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years without a write-up. I take that record seriously because I take the responsibility of transporting children seriously. I am including my work history as background, not as a substitute for reviewing this particular incident. I ask that the record reflect that I kept Amara on the bus because I did not see an adult to receive her and followed the district procedure for that situation.

To help prevent this from happening again, I respectfully ask that, consistent with the school’s directions for the stop, you wait where I can clearly see you on the bus side of the street. If you are waiting in a vehicle, please step out and make yourself visible before dismissal. I am not asking you to cross unsafely. If there is uncertainty about the safest place to wait, I would welcome the Transportation Office’s help in confirming an arrangement that works safely for everyone.

I am glad to continue driving Amara and want her daily ride to remain comfortable and positive. I also want you to feel confident that she is being cared for and that the release procedure is understood. My hope is that this statement and a review of the available footage will help resolve the concern respectfully and prevent another misunderstanding.

Sincerely,

[Your Name]  
School Bus Driver  
Bus 41, Route 9
